summary: Using a Dexcom G6 or ONE with AAPS, through xDrip or the Build Your Own Dexcom App (BYODA). Covers sensor and transmitter hints, which BG source to select in AAPS Configuration, matching xDrip settings, and troubleshooting.

sections.heading: Basics first
sections.summary: Points to the general CGM hygiene and sensor setting recommendations.

sections.heading: General hints for looping with G6 and ONE
sections.summary: Hardware advice: Firefly transmitters, sensor restarts, calibration and pre-soaking. No app labels.

sections.heading: If using G6 or ONE with xDrip
sections.summary: Using xDrip as the receiver for G6/ONE and selecting xDrip+ as the BG source in AAPS; explains that xDrip and the Dexcom app cannot share the transmitter.

sections.heading: If using G6 with Build Your Own Dexcom App
sections.summary: Installing BYODA in place of the official Dexcom app, entering the sensor code and transmitter serial, and granting the Dexcom app access in Android app permissions. The permission names are Android/Dexcom labels, not AAPS ones.

sections.heading: Settings for AAPS
sections.summary: Selecting the BYODA source (written here by its old name 'Dexcom App (patched)') in Configuration > BG Source, and re-selecting it to trigger the permission request if no values arrive.

sections.heading: Settings for xDrip
sections.summary: Settings inside xDrip when it receives BYODA broadcasts: the 640G/Eversense data source and starting a sensor in xDrip. xDrip labels only.

sections.heading: Dexcom G6/ONE specific troubleshooting
sections.summary: Points to the Troubleshooting part of the external xDrip Dexcom page; not an AAPS label.

sections.heading: General troubleshooting
sections.summary: Points to the general CGM troubleshooting page.

sections.heading: New transmitter with running sensor
sections.summary: How to swap a transmitter without damaging a running sensor; hardware only.
